## GitHub formula compatibility

These examples define the GitHub Docs dollar formula-expression surface
recognized by the `formula` extension. The wrapped delimiter/body text is the
payload handed to LaTeX/KaTeX.

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline $x+y$ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:7 literal="Inline " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:8..1:12 mode=embedded literal="x+y" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:13..1:17 literal=" end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Formula expressions parse as inline content inside table cells.

```````````````````````````````` example table
| expr |
| --- |
| $x+y$ |
.
Document scope=1:1..3:9 children=1
└── Table scope=1:1..3:9 alignments=[none] children=2
    ├── TableRow scope=1:1..1:8 isHeader=true children=1
    │   └── TableCell scope=1:2..1:7 children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:3..1:6 literal="expr" children=0
    └── TableRow scope=3:1..3:9 isHeader=false children=1
        └── TableCell scope=3:2..3:8 children=1
            └── Formula scope=3:3..3:7 mode=embedded literal="x+y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

GitHub's `$`...`$` form treats the backticks as formula delimiters, not as body
bytes.

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline $`x+y`$ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:19 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:19 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:7 literal="Inline " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:8..1:14 mode=embedded literal="x+y" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:15..1:19 literal=" end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
Escaped dollar $`\sqrt{\$4}`$ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:34 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:34 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:15 literal="Escaped dollar " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:16..1:29 mode=embedded literal="\\sqrt{\\$4}" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:30..1:34 literal=" end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Dollar formula delimiters do not open before whitespace.

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline $ x$ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:16 literal="Inline $ x$ end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Dollar formula delimiters do not close after whitespace.

```````````````````````````````` example
Inline $x $ end.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:16 literal="Inline $x $ end." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Dollar formula delimiters do not close before digits.

```````````````````````````````` example
Value $300B and ~$100B.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:23 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:23 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:23 literal="Value $300B and ~$100B." children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
$$x+y$$
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── FormulaBlock scope=1:1..1:7 literal="x+y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
$$
x+y
$$
.
Document scope=1:1..3:2 children=1
└── FormulaBlock scope=1:1..3:2 literal="x+y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

GitHub's ```formula fenced-code form is a formula block; the fence delimiters and
`formula` info string are not part of the formula body.

```````````````````````````````` example
```formula
x+y
```
.
Document scope=1:1..3:3 children=1
└── FormulaBlock scope=1:1..3:3 literal="x+y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unpaired dollar is ordinary punctuation for emphasis flanking: the
underscore after it still opens emphasis exactly as reference CommonMark
requires.

```````````````````````````````` example
foo$_bar_
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:4 literal="foo$" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:5..1:9 children=1
        └── Text scope=1:6..1:8 literal="bar" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Inline math carries the code-span padding rule: when the content both begins
and ends with a space and is not entirely spaces, one space is removed from
each end, so `$$ x $$` and `$$x$$` mean the same expression. The rule is
micromark-extension-math's, and it is the same one CommonMark applies to code
spans, which this parser already implemented there.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$ mid $$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:19 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:19 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:14 mode=standalone literal="mid" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:15..1:19 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Only one space is removed from each end, so interior padding is content.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$  x  $$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:19 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:19 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:14 mode=standalone literal=" x " children=0
    └── Text scope=1:15..1:19 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Content that is entirely spaces keeps them: the rule requires a non-space.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$ $$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:15 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:15 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:10 mode=standalone literal=" " children=0
    └── Text scope=1:11..1:15 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Two spaces are still entirely spaces, so neither is removed. This is the case
the rule's non-space requirement exists for: without it, padding would eat the
content of a formula that is deliberately blank.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$  $$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:11 mode=standalone literal="  " children=0
    └── Text scope=1:12..1:16 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A tab is not padding, so it is never the byte that gets stripped -- but it is
also not whitespace for the all-whitespace test, exactly as it is not for the
code span this rule is worded after. A body of spaces around a tab therefore
has content, and one space comes off each end.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$ 	 $$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:12 mode=standalone literal="\t" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:13..1:17 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The backtick form strips its backticks first, then the same rule applies.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $`  k  `$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:19 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:19 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:14 mode=embedded literal=" k " children=0
    └── Text scope=1:15..1:19 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Content shorter than two characters cannot be padded on both sides, so it is
left alone.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$x$$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:15 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:15 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:10 mode=standalone literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:11..1:15 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A line ending counts as a space for the rule, so inline math written across
lines carries the same expression as the single-line form.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$
x
$$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..3:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..3:7 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..3:2 mode=standalone literal="x" children=0
    └── Text scope=3:3..3:7 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Padding is removed only when it is present on both sides, so a space on one
side alone is content.

```````````````````````````````` example
text $$ mid$$ text
.
Document scope=1:1..1:18 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:18 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="text " children=0
    ├── Formula scope=1:6..1:13 mode=standalone literal=" mid" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:14..1:18 literal=" text" children=0
````````````````````````````````
